facts.statement: Eremochen lived during the Miocene epoch.
The genus Eremochen was described in 1961 by Pierce Brodkorb based on remains found in 1955 in the Juntura Formation of Oregon.
facts.quote: The genus was described in 1961 by Pierce Brodkorb, from remains discovered in 1955 in the Juntura Formation of Oregon.

facts.statement: The genus name Eremochen combines the Greek words for 'desert' and 'goose'.
facts.quote: The genus name, Eremochen, is composed of the Greek prefix Eremos-, meaning "desert", and -chen, meaning "goose".

facts.statement: The species name russelli honors the paleontologist Donald E. Russell.
facts.quote: The species name, russelli, was given to honour the paleontologist Donald E. Russell.

facts.statement: Eremochen lived between 12.5 and 4.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Serravallian to Zanclean (12.5 to 4.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: Eremochen belongs to the family Anatidae.
Eremochen is an extinct water bird belonging to the Anserinae subfamily.
facts.quote: Eremochen is an extinct genus of water bird, belonging to the Anserinae subfamily, which includes modern true geese and swans.

facts.statement: Eremochen was slightly smaller than the modern Atlantic Canada goose.
facts.quote: It was slightly smaller than the extant Atlantic Canada goose.
